Newshire (B50)

Survey-table region: Escann.

In a sentence: A halfling adventuring company settles in Escann and builds a new country with fields, teapots, and plant magic—only to discover that a harvest can consume people.

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 66/100 | Autocracy 52/100 | Magic–Artifice 95/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 95/100) | Pluralism 43/100. v2.1 values: Neutral (50/100), with a worsening trajectory. Resettling halflings, agricultural relief, and public life have clear positive value; instrumentalising locals and orcs, mage control over elections, and uncontrolled experiments undermine dignity, personhood, and restraint. War or magic alone is not a deduction.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Long (61 direct B50 definitions) | Verified version: local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high (halfling armies, phased unlocks, and the Verdancy) | Early pressure: Fairly high | Expansion: Medium-high.

How the Small Fellows found a home

In 1444, you do not control Newshire, but the halfling adventuring company Small Fellows (B10). Its leader, Dustin Smallknight, already appears in the history files. The company leaves the Small Country and enters post-Greentide Escann, seeking a place to live near Silverlake. Its initial challenges resemble those of other adventurers: clear the threats left by the Greentide, secure land, and meet the requirements for founding a country. But they want to build not another fortress of knights, but a halfling home with farms, markets, and tea. Only after B10 completes the relevant nation-founding decision does it become Newshire (B50), and the country's mission tree begins in earnest. The offline English Wiki's Newshire page is only an infobox and categories. A related halfling-history page connects Newshire's founding with migration after the failed Viswall Rebellion, but gives no exact departure date for the Small Fellows. The 1444 start and formation mechanics above therefore rest on local files.

From the setting's later perspective, Newshire is not an isolated pastoral idyll forever. The offline Wiki's Rogierian monarch list records that, when Rogier “the Young Owl” died in 1517, Newshire's halflings were already under his kingdom. The source does not specify whether this meant direct rule, vassalage, or another dependency. The national ideas also place the first appearance of house-sized pumpkins in the mid-16th century, after which they become Newshire's emblem. These are setting history and idea prose—not a requirement that players submit in 1517 or trigger a pumpkin event in a particular year.

The early country has the feel of a pastoral comedy: bring in fellow migrants, improve the fields, introduce bees, hold free markets, engage with other halflings and dwarves, and gradually form a “Newfoot” identity distinct from the homeland. The Small Fellows' old adventuring spirit becomes village self-government and agricultural production. The charm lies in this change of scale: you are not merely conquering territory, but giving displaced people a society they can call “ours.”

The mission text gives these everyday details real attention. Bees from home must adapt to Escann's climate, and farmers have to learn beekeeping. Tea is not only a trade good, but a symbol of communities sharing a new life. Cooperation with dwarves connects halfling pragmatism to craft and technology. This is not a purely peaceful “farm until the end” campaign: the apparently gentle development missions eventually feed, finance, and empower an army capable of unification wars.

The price of a harvest

The Chloromancers change the country. When the Crimson Deluge threatens agriculture, their guild saves fields through transformative magic. As their story intertwines with the Kettlebrook family, mages gradually take over military affairs, agriculture, and foreign policy. The country retains the appearance of festivals and elections, but later text says that popular votes increasingly struggle to influence senior rulers. Magic is no decoration here: soil, seeds, blood, and living bodies can all become political and military resources.

Militarily, halflings do not rely on conventional manpower advantages. Missions encourage mobilising farmers, reorganising the army, and unlocking plant-themed special mercenaries such as pods, nuts, and pumpkins. These forces serve the wars to unify Escann; they do not amount to an entirely different permanent plant-based military system, nor does every reward have identical strength in every version. Later, plant-growth magic spirals out of control and causes the Verdancy: rampant vegetation and creations turn on their makers, and Castanorian seeds and experiments become a crisis to resolve. Missions also explore life-magic reproduction and the difficult choice of leaving disaster sites to mages for research. These are possible campaign futures, not events that have already happened in 1444.

Newshire's values are therefore not “cute halflings are naturally good.” It does offer refugees a home, food, and public life, but its treatment of locals and orcs casts a shadow; later, mages weaken popular politics and uncontrolled experiments create large-scale danger. This article classifies it as Neutral: public benefit and real harm coexist. Reading only the pastoral surface or only the disaster ending misses the characters and conflicts in between.

The setting after the Verdancy cannot be reduced to “the mages win.” Event text says that the public blames the mages who once saved them, while some people continue researching seeds in dangerous areas and trying to use life magic to help families unable to conceive through ordinary means. The story does not declare life magic wholly beneficial or wholly harmful. Instead, it traces a technology from famine relief to political power and finally to a dangerous force that must be constrained. That is why the results card places Newshire very high in magical theme intensity without treating its values as unambiguously good.

Recommended for players who enjoy Escanni adventurers, agricultural development, magical failure, and family stories. If you want fast military snowballing, the halfling army and phased narrative may wear on you. One 2026 player post praises the theme but dislikes how the mercenary rewards feel; another enjoys the complete, symmetrical borders and pastoral expansion. These are experiences from different saves, not conclusions about current script strength.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Newshire (B50) — Newshireman Ideas

Set ID: B50_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B50
    }

Newshireman Traditions

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.10).

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

1. The New Small Country

Our homeland, the Small Country, is beset by war from all sides and split between foreign rulers. The idea of being free and able to rule ourselves was far from possible, until the miraculous sacrifice of Corin stopped the tide of the Greentide. Now us halflings have a land that we claim as a new Small Country, where we can once more live in peace.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

2. Orcward Forts

Despite the many forces of the Marcher Lords, the sacrifice of Corin, and the endless adventurers, Escann is still a land replete with orcs whose wish is to destroy all that is fair. Even though we wish to be left in peace, that does not mean that we cannot defend ourselves. The Orcward Forts were constructed to hold back these green-skinned monsters from our new home.

  • Fort maintenance: -15% (fort_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.15).

3. Peace, Love, and Prosperity Act

The Peace, Love, and Prosperity Act was signed in order to promote greater economic growth in our nation. Households of at least three children are incentivized with reduced taxes, and workshops that produce an increasing amount of goods produced each year are rewarded with a removal of sales tax on their goods.

  • Goods produced modifier: +10% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.10).

4. Newshire Sheriffs

Our dedication to peace and neighbourly conduct can only do so much when our neighbours are less than courteous. In fact, sometimes even young halflings can be rowdy. The Newshire Sheriffs are recruited from the most dedicated to our cause, they should be equally adequate at both stopping crime and the charge of gullible orcs with staff and stone.

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.10).

5. Enormous Pumpkins

Sometime in the mid sixteenth century a strange phenomenon occurred in Newshire. Pumpkins the size of homes grew from our vines, able to feed a family for weeks. Every year since then, massive pumpkins have grown in Newshire, and we are known far and wide for our equally grand pumpkin pie.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1.0).

6. Honest Words and Smiles

Throughout the world nations know that Newshire is honest to its word and mission: a new home for halflings, and the continuation of peace for our people. They know that we have no other secrets or ambitions that may tarnish our standing.

  • Improve relations: +20% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.2).

7. Halfling Heroes

Many years after the Greentide, stories are told about our heroes of old who cleaved the path so that we could live in peace in our Newshire. Some of these heroes still remain, and others still are created in the mission of preserving our nation. It would do well for us to listen to these heroes, for they alone know the vision that our halfling nation needs.

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -15% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.15).

  • Global trade power: +15% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.15).
